item.title: Quantum dot lasers may unlock next era of AI optical interconnects
item.description: A misconception about quantum dot lasers (QDLs) is they’re poised to replace indium phosphide (InP) technology. But InP externally modulated lasers (EMLs) will continue serving optical networking and datacom applications, while QDLs emerge for applications that require power efficiency, thermal resilience, and integration density.

item.description: As inertial fusion energy moves from scientific breakthrough to commercial reality, scalable and cost-effective laser hardware is the key to moving from laboratory demonstrations to viable power plants—and low-cost, fusion-grade laser diodes can be manufactured at scale in Arizona to anchor a global inertial fusion energy supply chain.

item.title: Quantum interference traps electron waves in metal for first time
item.description: Ever since quantum mechanics first described particles, like electrons, as rippling waves, researchers have wondered if those waves could be trapped in place. Writing today in Science a century later, a team of Columbia University researchers reports waves of electrons becoming trapped for the first time in a metal called Pd₅AlI₂.
